Subject: Quick recap + DPA / SCC questions after today's demo

Hi Sarah / Matt —

Thanks again for the demo time today — really appreciated the clear overview of your ingestion patterns and the latency profile you need for enrichment workflows. A quick recap and next steps on the privacy/compliance side so we can move toward contracting: 

- Your primary ask: Redwood will process customer PII as part of enrichment pipelines (names + accounts). You indicated FinOptima will be the data controller.
- Immediate asks from your side: copy of our SOC 2 snapshot and DPA + SCC module preference so procurement can route the contract.

To keep things moving, can you confirm these two items:
1) FinOptima's preference for SCC module (Module 1 vs Module 2) or whether you want Redwood to accept the EU Standard Contractual Clauses via the Redrafted SCCs (we can recommend a module based on role alignment).
2) Procurement contact (email) for DocuSign / order form.

I've attached the DPA template we normally start from and our security questionnaire stub so you can see the fields we'll need to fill. If you can share a SOC 2 snapshot (or point me to a Drive link) we'll send the formal evidence package and legal can start SCC module selection.

Planned next step: internal legal review (looping in Laura and Ben) once you confirm SCC preference / provide procurement contact.

Thanks — will keep this light on coordination.

Best,
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Jonas / Laura —

Thanks for the context and for sharing the attachments. Quick guidance from legal/security: 

1) Controller/Processor: if FinOptima will be controller and Redwood is purely processing (no independent control decisions), we should aim to accept controller -> processor language and sign a DPA with Redwood as processor. That aligns with typical SaaS setups and keeps liability bounded.

2) SCC module: recommend we propose the Redrafted SCCs using the Module 2 approach for processor-to-controller transfers (this matches their preference). We will include the optional Processor Annex for subprocessors and a data flow diagram.

3) SOC 2: we need Redwood's SOC 2 snapshot to share with FinOptima; I'll prepare a short evidence pack (SOC2-index + link) that we can send. Jonas, please confirm you will circulate that to Sarah and procurement.

4) DPA redlines to expect: minimal changes around liability caps and audit frequency; procurement teams sometimes ask to add audit rights language — we'll push back to a reasonable scope (annual audits with notice).

If you can share the planned order form / expected volume, we can include a tailored annex for retention and deletion. I'll draft SCC language and the Processor Annex today and share.

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
